g.meta.title: User Guide — Rankly
g.meta.desc: How to install and use Rankly: tracking App Store keyword ranks, reading the table, running the ASO analysis, multi-country analysis, updates, data storage and troubleshooting.
g.lead: From installing the app to reading the analysis and keeping your data under control.
g.install.2: Open the DMG and drag Rankly into the Applications folder.
g.install.3: Eject the DMG and open Rankly from Applications or Launchpad.
g.install.req: Requirements: macOS 14 Sonoma or later, on Apple silicon or Intel Macs.
g.first.1: Rankly is signed and notarized by Apple, so macOS may ask once whether you want to open an app downloaded from the internet. Click Open.
g.first.2: There's no account and no setup. You start with an empty sidebar — add your first app to begin.
g.add.1: Click Add App (the + button in the sidebar).
g.add.2: Type the app's name, its App Store ID (e.g. id1234567890 or just the digits) or paste its App Store link.
g.add.3: Choose the country (storefront) to track — 53 are available — and press Search.
g.add.4: Click Add next to the right result. Turn on Add as competitor if it isn't your own app.
g.add.5: You can track any app — yours or anyone else's. Each tracked app lives in the sidebar with its keyword count.
g.kw.1: Select an app, type into the keyword field at the top of the Keywords tab and press Add. Separate several keywords with commas to add them at once:
g.kw.2: Rankly checks each new keyword right away. Right-click keywords to refresh, copy or delete the selection.
g.col.keyword: The search term, exactly as a user would type it into the App Store.
g.col.rank: Your position in the iPhone App Store search results for that country. Rankly reads the top 250; >250 means the app isn't in them.
g.col.change: How many places the rank moved since yesterday. Green arrow = up, red arrow = down.
g.col.popularity: ~5–100. An estimate based on how early (after how many letters) and how high the term appears in App Store autocomplete. It is not Apple's Search Ads popularity score.
g.col.difficulty: 0–100. How hard the term is to rank for, based on how established the top-10 apps are (their rating counts) and how many of them use the term in their name.
g.col.trend: A sparkline of the recent rank history.
g.refresh.1: Ranks are refreshed automatically once a day: when Rankly starts and the data is older than today, and then with an hourly check while the app is running. One result per keyword per day is stored in the history. With the menu bar extra on, Rankly keeps running after you close the main window, so the daily refresh still happens.
g.refresh.2: To refresh manually, click the refresh button in the toolbar or press <kbd>⌘</kbd><kbd>R</kbd> (refresh all ranks). A progress counter shows how many keywords are done. Requests are deliberately paced, so large lists take a little while.
g.detail.1: Select a keyword to open its detail panel:
g.detail.2: Rank History — a chart of the daily ranks (needs at least two days of data).
g.detail.3: Apps ranking for this keyword — the top 30 apps with their rating and number of ratings.
g.detail.4: Track — adds that app as a competitor in one click so you can follow its ranks too. Apps you already follow show Tracking.
g.sugg.1: Click Keyword Suggestions (lightbulb) in the toolbar, enter a seed word and press Find. Rankly lists related searches from App Store autocomplete with an estimated popularity and a difficulty score. Add the ones you like with a click.
g.an.1: Switch to the Analysis tab and click Start Analysis. Rankly extracts candidate keywords from the app's name, subtitle and description, expands them with autocomplete and searches each in the App Store. It takes about 1–2 minutes; results are saved per country and you can re-run it anytime with Re-analyze.
g.an.p1: Every candidate term where the app appears in the results, with its rank, popularity and difficulty.
g.an.h2: Name & subtitle words you don't rank for
g.an.p2: Words that already sit in your most valuable metadata but don't bring you into the results — strong candidates for a rethink.
g.an.p3: Discovered automatically: apps that keep appearing near the top for your keywords, from the same category. Competitors you track are always included. Each shows its rating, how many keywords it shares with you and how many it ranks in the top 50 for. Click Track to follow one.
g.an.p4: Keywords where competitors rank in the top 30 but you don't. They're scored by popularity, difficulty and how many competitors use them. Searches for brand or app names are filtered out. Click Track to add a keyword to your list.
g.an.p5: A ready-to-paste, comma-separated 100-character keyword field for App Store Connect, built from your best terms. Words already in your name or subtitle aren't repeated (Apple indexes those anyway). Click Copy and paste it into App Store Connect.
g.an.note: Apple never publishes an app's hidden keyword field. Rankly doesn't guess it — it finds the keywords the app really ranks for.
g.mc.1: In the Analysis tab, click Multi-country Analysis….
g.mc.2: Language matching — Rankly reads the languages the app is localized in from the App Store and pre-selects the storefronts that search in those languages. Other countries are listed separately: the app shows in its default language there, so ranking is usually weak.
g.mc.3: Skip countries analysed in the last 24 hours — keep this on to avoid repeating fresh work.
g.mc.4: Click Start Analysis. Countries are analysed one by one in the background, each with its localized name and description. The sheet shows an estimated duration; it's slow on purpose so Apple doesn't block you.
g.mc.5: When done, switch the scope to All countries for a per-country overview (keywords you rank for, how many in the top 10, opportunities) and the best opportunities across all countries.
g.mc.6: Resume after a block — if Apple temporarily blocks search, the run pauses and shows how many countries are finished. After the indicated time, click Continue with Remaining. Failed countries can be retried with Retry Failed.
g.mb.1: Rankly adds an icon to the macOS menu bar. Click it for a compact view of your own apps, without opening the main window:
g.mb.3: Top movers — the keywords that moved the most since yesterday.
g.mb.4: Your keywords with their current rank and change. If you have several apps, switch between them from the menu.
g.mb.5: Buttons to open Rankly, check for updates, open Settings and quit.
g.mb.6: While the menu bar extra is on, closing the main window keeps Rankly running, so daily ranks keep updating in the background. Turn it off with Show in menu bar in Settings (⌘,). Enable Launch at login there to have Rankly start with your Mac.
g.up.1: Rankly updates itself with Sparkle. By default it checks for a new version automatically once a day. You can check right away with Rankly → Check for Updates…, the download button in the menu bar extra, or Check Now in Settings.
g.up.2: In Settings (<kbd>⌘</kbd><kbd>,</kbd>) you can turn automatic checks off, or let Rankly download and install updates automatically.
g.up.3: Every update is signed and notarized and downloaded from GitHub Releases. The update check only fetches the release feed — no system profile or usage data is sent.
g.data.1: Everything stays on your Mac, inside Rankly's sandbox container:
g.data.2: SwiftData store — tracked apps, keywords and rank history.
g.data.3: Analysis results — one JSON file per app and country in Library/Application Support/Rankly/analysis/.
g.data.4: Nothing is synced or uploaded anywhere.
g.un.1: If you enabled Launch at login, turn it off in Settings. Then quit Rankly — use the power button in the menu bar extra, or ⌘Q.
g.un.2: Move Rankly from Applications to the Trash.
g.un.3: In Finder choose Go → Go to Folder…, enter ~/Library/Containers/ and move the com.ardasenturk.rankly folder to the Trash. This deletes all tracked apps, keywords, history and analyses.
g.ts.p1: Apple briefly blocks the search endpoint for a network that sends too many requests. Rankly then stops all searches for one hour (retrying would only extend the block) and shows when it will continue. It also doubles the spacing between requests for the future (up to 8 seconds). Just wait — refreshes and analyses resume afterwards.
g.ts.p2: The app isn't in the top 250 results for that keyword in that country. Check that you're looking at the right storefront and that the app is available there. New keywords often need time — and metadata changes — to start ranking.
g.ts.p3: The App Store asked Rankly to slow down. Rankly waits and retries automatically with longer pauses. If the error remains, try again a little later.
g.ts.p4: Open an issue on GitHub with your macOS version, Rankly version and what you saw.

meta.title: Rankly — Free App Store keyword rank tracker for Mac
meta.desc: Rankly is a free, open-source macOS app that tracks where any iPhone app ranks in App Store search — daily, in 53 countries, with automatic ASO analysis. No account, no subscription, no server.
hero.lead: Rankly tracks where any iPhone app ranks in App Store search — in 53 countries, with history, competitors and an automatic keyword analysis. A free alternative to paid ASO tools. No account, no subscription, no server.
demo.aria: Animated preview of Rankly's keyword table: keywords with their rank, daily change, popularity, difficulty and trend.
demo.note: Illustration with sample data. Popularity is an estimate.
stats.chars: character keyword field, written for you
features.title1: Everything you pay ASO tools for.
features.lead: Rankly reads the real iPhone App Store search results, so the ranks you see are the ranks your users see.
f1.title: Daily keyword rank tracking
f1.text: Add any app by name, App Store ID or link, then add keywords. Rankly checks the top 250 search results once a day in 53 countries and keeps the full history.
f2.title: Popularity & difficulty
f2.text: Popularity (~5–100) is estimated from App Store autocomplete. Difficulty (0–100) comes from how established the top-10 apps are and how many put the term in their name.
f3.title: Competitor tracking
f3.text: See every app ranking for a keyword — the top 30 with ratings — and start tracking any of them in one click.
f4.title: Keyword suggestions
f4.text: Find related searches straight from App Store autocomplete, each with its popularity and difficulty, and add them with a click.
f5.title: Automatic ASO analysis
f5.text: In about 1–2 minutes Rankly finds the keywords you rank for, discovers your competitors, scores opportunities and suggests a 100-character keyword field.
f6.title: Multi-country analysis
f6.text: Rankly reads your app's languages from the App Store, pre-selects the matching storefronts and analyses each one with its localized name and description.
f7.title: Menu bar extra
f7.text: A compact view of your tracked keywords — top movers and current ranks — right from the menu bar, without opening the main window.
f8.title: Automatic updates
f8.text: Signed and notarized builds from GitHub Releases, delivered through Sparkle. You always run the latest version.
f9.title: Gentle on Apple
f9.text: Requests are paced. If Apple temporarily blocks search (HTTP 403), Rankly pauses for an hour instead of hammering the servers.

step1.title: Extract candidates
step1.text: Candidate keywords are pulled from your app's name, subtitle and description, then expanded with App Store autocomplete.
step2.title: Search the App Store
step2.text: Each candidate is searched in the real App Store to see where you rank — and which words from your name or subtitle you don't rank for.
step3.title: Discover competitors
step3.text: Apps in your category that keep showing up at the top for your keywords become your competitor set — automatically.
step4.title: Score opportunities
step4.text: Keywords where competitors rank in the top 30 but you don't are scored by popularity, difficulty and how many competitors use them. Brand and app-name searches are filtered out.
step5.title: Get your keyword field
step5.text: A suggested 100-character keyword field for App Store Connect, without repeating words already in your name or subtitle. One click to copy.

pv.lead: No account, no analytics, no tracking. The developer runs no server and receives no data.
pv1.title: No account
pv1.text: Download, open, start tracking. Nothing to sign up for.
pv2.title: No server
pv2.text: Rankly talks to Apple's App Store directly. There's no Rankly backend.
pv3.title: No analytics
pv3.text: No tracking, no ads, no cookies. Not in the app, not on this site.
pv4.title: Local data
pv4.text: Apps, keywords, history and analyses live in the app's sandbox on your Mac.
faq.title: Questions, answered
faq1.a: Yes. Rankly is open source under the MIT license. There's no subscription, no trial, no paid tier and no account.
faq2.a: No. Apple only shares its search popularity with Apple Search Ads customers. Rankly's popularity (~5–100) is an estimate based on how early and how high a term appears in App Store autocomplete. Use it to compare keywords, not as an absolute figure.
faq3.q: Why does it need no account?
faq3.a: Because there's nothing to log in to. Rankly asks Apple's public App Store endpoints directly from your Mac and stores everything locally. There's no Rankly server holding your data.
faq4.a: Rankly paces its requests to stay polite. If Apple still temporarily blocks search for your network (HTTP 403), Rankly pauses for an hour instead of retrying, which would only extend the block. Ranking checks simply continue later.
faq5.q: Is it on the Mac App Store?
faq5.a: No. Rankly is distributed through GitHub Releases as a signed and notarized DMG, and keeps itself up to date with Sparkle.
faq6.a: Rankly checks iPhone App Store search results, the top 250 per keyword, in any of 53 countries. If your app isn't in the top 250, it's shown as >250.
faq7.q: Can it show a competitor's keyword field?
faq7.a: No tool can — Apple never publishes the hidden 100-character keyword field. Rankly shows the keywords a competitor actually ranks for, which is what matters.
faq8.a: No. Rankly is an independent project. It uses Apple's public but undocumented App Store endpoints, which Apple may change at any time.
cta.lead: Free, open source, and private by design.
p.meta.title: Privacy Policy — Rankly
p.meta.desc: Rankly's privacy policy: no account, no analytics, no tracking. All data stays on your Mac. The only network requests go to Apple's App Store and to GitHub for updates.
p.lead: The short version: Rankly has no account, no analytics, no tracking and no server. The developer never receives your data.
p.sum.1: This policy covers the Rankly macOS app and this website (rankly.ardasnturk.com). Both are operated by Arda Sentürk (“we”, “the developer”).
p.sum.3: No analytics, no tracking, no advertising, no cookies in the app.
p.sum.4: The developer runs no server and receives no data from the app.
p.sum.5: Everything you track is stored locally on your Mac.
p.collect.1: Nothing. Rankly does not collect, transmit, sell or share any personal data with the developer or with any third party for analytics or advertising. There is no crash reporting or telemetry built into the app.
p.net.1: To work, Rankly connects directly from your Mac to only these services:
p.net.2: Rankly uses Apple's public App Store endpoints at search.itunes.apple.com (search ranking and autocomplete suggestions) and itunes.apple.com (app lookup). These requests contain only what is needed for the lookup: search terms, App Store app IDs and storefront/country codes.
p.net.3: Like any App Store request, Apple can see your IP address. Apple's own privacy policy applies to these requests. Rankly is not affiliated with Apple.
p.net.4: Rankly uses the Sparkle framework to check for updates. It downloads the update feed https://rankly.ardasnturk.com/appcast.xml (hosted on GitHub Pages) and, when you install an update, the update file from GitHub Releases. GitHub can see your IP address for these downloads; GitHub's privacy statement applies. No system profile or usage information is sent with update checks.
p.store.1: All tracked apps, keywords, rank history and analysis results are stored locally in the app's sandbox container:
p.store.2: This data never leaves your Mac through Rankly. Deleting the app's container folder removes everything. See the uninstall guide.
p.web.1: rankly.ardasnturk.com is a static site hosted on GitHub Pages. It uses no analytics and no cookies. Your language choice is remembered in your browser's local storage and never sent anywhere.
p.web.2: GitHub, as the host, processes server logs such as your IP address to deliver the pages. The site loads fonts from Google Fonts, so Google may receive your IP address when you visit; see Google's privacy policy.
p.child.1: Rankly is a tool for app developers and marketers and is not directed at children. Since it collects no personal data, it collects none from children either.
p.chg.1: If this policy changes, the updated version will be published on this page with a new effective date. Significant changes will also be noted in the release notes on GitHub.
p.contact.1: Questions about privacy? Open an issue at github.com/ardasnturk/rankly/issues.
